issues.legal_issue: A cheating charge requires dishonest deception that induces the alleged victim to act or deliver property, and cannot be sustained where the alleged victim was not dishonestly induced.
The absence of evidence that the accused knowingly agreed to deceive the alleged victim defeats a charge of criminal conspiracy.
A party with an available statutory revision remedy cannot bypass its limitation period by invoking the High Court’s inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The discharge of the accused was justified where the evidence did not support the alleged offences of cheating or criminal conspiracy.
